sections.heading: Glamsterdam Devnet 8 and Devnet 9 Planning
sections.summary: Devnet 8 is stable; devnet 9 will be a non-finality devnet launching once all clients have trunk branches ready, running about 4 days.
sections.body:
- Devnet 8 is running smoothly with ~10 blobs and 100-150 transactions per slot and close to 100% participation; occasional missing payloads were traced to outdated client releases
- All clients need to merge fixes into trunk branches; once deployed on the devnet, fuzzing will continue
- Devnet 9 will be a non-finality devnet, expected to run at most 4 days
  - Plan: one day on SilaFulu with 100% participation through fork transition, then Toni can start attack testing, followed by non-finality period and recovery attempt
  - Will include 20-25,000 builder deposits (some invalid) and ~3-4 million validators (~600-700 MB state)
- Toni raised concern about needing a separate devnet for attack testing distinct from non-finality stress, but Barnabas indicated devnet 9 can accommodate both sequentially

sections.heading: Glamsterdam Testnet and SilaMainnet Timeline
sections.summary: September 28 proposed for SilaSepolia fork, October 26 for Hoodi, with ~30-day security and ecosystem windows targeting early December sila-mainnet.
sections.body:
- September 28th proposed for SilaSepolia Glamsterdam fork, October 26th for Hoodi; these dates were floated on ACDC last week and will be confirmed on next ACDC
- Approximately 30-day security audit window after testnet forks, then 30-day window for L2s and DAOs to prepare
- This brings the sila-mainnet fork to approximately end of November / early December
- Lido was mentioned as potentially wanting a few more days for SilaSepolia, but no Lido representative spoke on the call; topic can be raised at next ACDC
- No opposition voiced to the proposed timeline

sections.heading: History Expiry Retention Window Alignment
sections.summary: All clients agree to align on the CL block retention window of 33,000 epochs; Kev will update SIP-4444 and follow up with Geth.
sections.body:
- Kevaundray proposed updating SIP-4444 to document the retention window rather than creating a new SIP
- Client readiness: Nimbus has implemented it; Nethermind has implemented it; Reth says next release; Ethrex has a PR up and is testing; Erigon will look into it; Geth has agreed but no implementation update given (no Geth representative on call)
- Currently 2TB nodes are near capacity at 1.5-1.8 TB; launching Glamsterdam without expiring history could exhaust storage
- Kev will create a PR to update SIP-4444 to specify 33,000 epochs and will follow up with Geth async

sections.heading: Deposit Contract PQ Readiness
sections.summary: Multiple strategies discussed for upgrading the deposit contract for post-quantum; no decision reached, with Ben Adams preferring to bundle changes with PBT migration.
sections.body:
- Kevaundray outlined strategies: deploy a new deposit contract, modify the old one via irregular state transition, use a precompile, or a deposit opcode
- lightclient expressed light preference for an irregular state transition
- Ben Adams opposed setting a precedent of modifying deployed contracts, but would accept it if bundled with a massive state reorganization like the binary tree (PBT) migration, since that is already an extraordinary irregular state transition
- Discussion in chat about whether validators using BLS keys would need to exit/re-enter or could be migrated at fork time
  - Two-fork approach suggested: first deploy new contract supporting both BLS and PQ, give ecosystem time to switch, then disable BLS at PQ fork
  - potuz argued it's acceptable to let users lose money if the soak period is months/years, no need for irregular state transition
- No concrete decision reached; Kev to continue async discussions

sections.heading: eth_simulateV1 Specification Gaps
sections.summary: eth_simulateV1 spec is not updated for simulated blocks, causing client disagreements; Chase asked clients to review and comment async.
sections.body:
- Chase Wright reported that eth_simulate has not been updated to specify behavior for simulated blocks
- All clients currently disagree on what to include in simulated block responses
- Issue linked: [eth_simulateV1 issues](https://github.com/sila-chain/execution-apis/issues/868)
- Follow-up will happen asynchronously; clients asked to review and comment on the issue

sections.heading: SIP-8037 Self-Destruct Gas Refill Modification
sections.summary: Request to restore self-destruct gas refill in SIP-8037 was declined for Glamsterdam due to late timing; ephemeral contract solution deferred to Hegota.
sections.body:
- Milos Costantini raised [SIP-8037 PR](https://github.com/sila-chain/SIPs/pull/12249) requesting restoration of gas refill for self-destruct, arguing ephemeral contracts (used for intents, routing, bridging) would see ~7-10x gas cost increase without it
- Maria Silva (8037 author) explained the refill was removed for simplicity in testing, reduced spec complexity, and alignment with the direction of deprecating self-destruct
  - Noted current usage is ~1,500 accounts/day created and self-destructed in same transaction, accounting for ~62 MB state/year
  - Stressed that while gas cost rises in relative terms, base fee decrease from gas limit increase means end-user fees won't rise proportionally
- Milos argued this is an emerging paradigm for signerless addresses and intent protocols, and the overhead of ~200,000 gas per transaction is significant
- Consensus: too late to change Glamsterdam spec; requires spec changes, client code changes, and additional testing
- Decision: TCREATE opcode (SIP-8360) kept as a PFI placeholder for a Hegota solution; Milos, Helcomine (ABC), and 8037 authors urged to collaborate on a solution within the next 2-4 weeks
- Ansgar warned that deferring to Hegota doesn't mean waiting months — SIP champions must advocate within the Hegota scoping window or the SIP won't be included
- Danno Ferrin noted SELFDESTRUCT was deprecated in SilaShanghai (SIP-6049) almost 4 years ago and new uses should not be accommodated

sections.heading: Hegota Scoping Process and PFI Decisions
sections.summary: Client preferences due by September 9; SIP-7609 and SIP-8058 dropped from PFI; SIP-8360 (TCREATE) retained as placeholder.
sections.body:
- EL client teams asked to submit Hegota non-headliner preferences to facilitators by September 9th (24 hours before next ACDE on September 10th)
- SIP champions must attend the next 3-4 ACDE calls (Sep 10, 24, Oct 8, 22) for Hegota scoping; absence may result in SIP rejection
- [SIP-7609](https://sips.sila.org/EIPS/sip-7609) (decrease base cost of TLOAD/TSTORE): no one spoke for it; dropped from PFI
- [SIP-8058](https://sips.sila.org/EIPS/sip-8058) (contract bytecode deduplication discount): Ben Adams noted this is superseded by SETCODEFROM which achieves the same goal more generally; dropped from PFI
- [SIP-8360](https://github.com/sila-chain/SIPs/pull/12073) (TCREATE opcode): retained as PFI placeholder for the ephemeral contract / self-destruct gas refill problem discussed earlier
- Pooja Ranjan raised open PRs for Glamsterdam and Hegota Meta SIPs (7773 and 8081) needing author approvals; urged Meta SIP authors to review and approve or comment on pending PRs to avoid CI conflicts and keep upgrade information current

sections.heading: SIP-8304 Trustless Log and Transaction Index Demo
sections.summary: Zsolt demonstrated a working REST API with proofs for SIP-8304's trustless log index, urging clients to evaluate it for Hegota inclusion.
sections.body:
- Zsolt Felföldi presented progress on [SIP-8304](https://sips.sila.org/EIPS/sip-8304), a trustless log and transaction index, with a live demo against a sila-mainnet node
- Design is significantly simpler and more efficient than the previous SIP-7745 approach
- API is REST-based (similar to Beacon API format) with JSON and binary encoding, supporting:
  - Provable canonical block hashes from entire history
  - Transaction hash inclusion/exclusion proofs
  - Efficient log queries with AND/OR search patterns and cross-log pattern matching within transactions
- Proofs are anchored in state via an index contract storing root hashes of binary tree index tables
  - Simple queries (e.g., first occurrence of an address) produce proofs under 100 KB
  - Query pagination and server-side limits protect against overload
- Demo showed inclusion and exclusion proofs for the wrapped SIL contract address using a dummy index contract on sila-mainnet
- Zsolt argued this infrastructure could enable contracts to use logs more for state representation and improve cross-chain communication
- Requested clients evaluate and rank it for Hegota; proof size and speed results described as better than initially expected

sections.heading: SIP-8141 Frames SFI Decision and 8130 Convergence
sections.summary: SIP-8141 (Frames) moved to SFI with broad client support; spec changes remain expected as collaboration with SIP-8130 (Base/L2s) continues weekly.
sections.body:
- Derek Chiang (SIP-8141 co-author) provided update: 8130 and 8141 authors established a communication channel and spent significant time exploring convergence
  - Best outcome: shared transaction type that is flexible like frames but supports opinionated systems like 8130
  - Fallback outcome: two transaction types but same account at same address works across L1 and L2 chains
  - Collaboration timeboxed to 2-4 weeks to avoid blocking either L1 or L2 timelines
- Base timeline: 8130 scheduled for end of September launch, but can pull it from their fork late if needed
- Vitalik outlined the design space dimensions where convergence is possible:
  - Keystore in account header vs. contract (header is more efficient)
  - Splitting authenticating code from non-authenticating code (core 8130 feature, could be added to 8141)
  - Transaction type unification (one master type defining actions and dependencies)
  - Precompiles vs. opcodes (precompiles enable cross-chain compatibility via contract wrapping)
  - Suggested SFI-ing 8141 and continuing refinements afterward
- On post-quantum readiness: Vitalik explained 8141 naturally supports Sphinx Minus (hash-based, no new precompiles needed) and a future Stark mempool aggregation approach for efficient PQ signature verification
- Ethrex (Tomás Arjovsky) voiced concern about private side-channel discussions being presented as official outcomes; stated ethrex supports 8141 because it provides building blocks without enshrining a particular approach, unlike the more opinionated 8130
- Nethermind (Stavros) also supported moving 8141 to SFI, arguing it provides certainty for both L1 and L2 teams
- Besu confirmed support for 8141
- Erigon said they haven't looked at the SIPs in detail and had no view
- Decision: SIP-8141 (Frames) moved to SFI
  - Ansgar's caveat accepted: SFI status must not be used as argument against making radical spec changes going forward
  - AA breakout calls will move to weekly cadence (Tuesdays 14:00 UTC) for the next month to month and a half
- Hegota scoping for AA headliner status targeted for completion by DEVCON (November 3rd)
- Multiple chat participants urged all AA-related discussion to happen on SIL R&D rather than private channels
